::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Application of Rolle's theorem and determinant](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3302694/application-of-rolles-theorem-and-determinant), asked by [Abhishek Kumar](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/660691/abhishek-kumar) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2019-07-24; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> $f(x) =
> \begin{vmatrix}
>  \sin^3x & \sin^3 a & \sin^3 b \\ 
>  xe^x & ae^a & be^b\\
> \frac{x}{1+x^2} & \frac{a}{1+a^2} & \frac{b}{1+b^2}
> \end{vmatrix}$<br>
> Where $0<a<b<2π$ then show that the equation $f^{'}(x)=0$  has atlest one root in the interval $(a,b)$
>
> **My approach**
> First try to differentiate the give determinant and find that $f^{'}(x)=0$ then I apply the Rolle's theorem to solve the question. 
>
> I face the difficulty in differentiate the determinant.
:::

Let $\mathbf{c}$ be the vector-valued function which takes $x$ to $\left<\sin^3x,xe^x,x/(1+x^2)\right>$.  Then $f(x)$ is the scalar triple product of $\mathbf{c}(x)$, $\mathbf{c}(a)$, and $\mathbf{c}(b)$:
$$f(x) = \mathbf{c}(x) \cdot \left(\mathbf{c}(a) \times \mathbf{c}(b)\right)$$
Because the cross product of two vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is orthogonal to each of the individual vectors, $f(a) = f(b) = 0$.  So by Rolle's Theorem there exists a point $x$ between $a$ and $b$ where $f'(x) = 0$.
